checked_obligation: Under the forward-implication assumption that a is a primitive root modulo the prime p, verify that a^((p-1)/2) is congruent to -1 modulo p.
reason: Since a has order p-1 modulo p, Fermat's theorem gives a^(p-1)≡1 mod p, while a^((p-1)/2)≢1 mod p because (p-1)/2<p-1. Factoring a^(p-1)-1 and using primality of p shows that a^((p-1)/2)≡1 or -1 mod p; the first alternative is excluded, proving the claim.
